aspect: EXAMPLE - Ontario health coverage refused on a waiting period that no longer exists
description: Ontario eliminated the three-month OHIP wait for most people in 2020, so coverage is immediate for eligible applicants. A denial based on a 'waiting period' in Ontario is therefore likely to be a clerk error - but the applicant leaves uninsured either way.
money_note: Uninsured medical costs during the gap.
energy_note: Uninsured because of a rule that was abolished years ago.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the rule is not published, so the clerk invents one
description: Ontario does not publish explicit requirements for people on maintained status and instead tells them to contact ServiceOntario to determine eligibility - meaning front-line staff work without clear published rules, which is a recognised source of wrongful refusals.
energy_note: No rule to point at, so no way to be right.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the service that exists but is not online
description: In Quebec, extending RAMQ coverage on maintained status may be possible but is not offered online - it has to be arranged by telephone. A clerk unfamiliar with it refuses outright, and the applicant has no way to know the option existed.
energy_note: Refused a thing you were never told existed.

description: Children under 18, recognised refugees and citizens of ten bilateral-agreement countries are exempt from the Quebec waiting period. Each exemption is a rule a busy counter may not apply.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the clock starts when they say it starts
description: RAMQ eligibility runs from the registration date provided all documents are submitted; a missing document pushes the start date back. A document wrongly deemed missing costs months of coverage retroactively.
energy_note: Backdated exclusion for a document you did provide.

aspect: EXAMPLE - no reimbursement for the gap
description: RAMQ does not reimburse care received before the eligibility start date. If the refusal was wrong and is later corrected, the medical bills incurred meanwhile are still yours.

The advice that works: get the refusal in writing with the specific reason, escalate past the counter, and file a written review with new evidence under the relevant health insurance act. All of which requires knowing you were wrongly refused in the first place.
energy_note: Remedy available only to those who already know the rule.

aspect: SCENARIO - uninsured for five months by mistake
description: Omid lands in Ontario in 2023 on a work permit. The ServiceOntario clerk tells him there is a three-month wait. There has not been one since 2020. He buys private cover for three months, then lets it lapse, then waits two more months before a colleague tells him to go back. In month four he has appendicitis: CAD 11,400.
energy_note: A surgery billed to you because of a rule that was abolished.
